newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INTERVIEW - HK&S Hotels looks beyond HK.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - HK&S Hotels looks beyond HK.

text.p: Luxury hotelier Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd is confident its home base of Hong Kong will make a smooth transition to Chinese rule later this year, but says the company's future growth lies outside the territory.

"Logically, our developments are now going to be geographically dispersed," Douglas Webster, director in charge of finance and corporate services, told Reuters on Thursday. "We also want to consolidate our position in Southeast Asia."
The group has hotels under development in Bangkok, Jakarta and Sydney and the company is in the early stage of discussion with potential Chinese partners in Shanghai, Webster said.
"I would expect that in the not too distant future we would return to Shanghai, to develop a mixed-use complex that would include a hotel, with Chinese partners," said Webster.
The group once owned five hotels in Shanghai, but sold its China interests by the mid-1950s.
The company is also interested in Tokyo.
Webster said the group was in a strong financial position, with a net debt to equity ratio of 16 percent.
"We have fairly good cash flow every year, plus our borrowing capacity, which is quite strong, so we are in a position to undertake projects as they come along," he said.
Webster said Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels was confident about the reversion of its home base, Hong Kong, to China at midnight on June 30.
"The people that planned for this day know it will be a relatively seamless transition," he said. "Over time there will be changes."
Webster said he was very optimistic about the future.
"We are a Hong Kong company, therefore in a very short time we will be a Chinese company," said Webster. "We are quite happy with this situation."

"I think the combination of the ability of Hong Kong to provide financial services and all the other things that Hong Kong does very well, couple that with the sleepy giant of China and the 1.2 billion (people) and you have an unstoppable combination," he said.

Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels has about 80 percent of its assets in Hong Kong. The remainder of its wholly-owned operations are chiefly in the United States, including the Peninsula New York and the group's latest acquisition, the Quail Lodge resort complex in California.
On the group's Sydney hotel and residential development, the target of much local criticism, the company would be submitting new plans to the authorities in a few weeks, Webster said.

After months of protests from Sydney residents, the company was redesigning the project, eliminating one of the two originally planned apartment blocks, and planning a taller but narrower hotel block.
Opponents of the group's original plans said the development was too high and too wide and spoiled views of Sydney's famous Opera House and neighbouring botanical gardens.
"We have been interested in Sydney and looking at this particular site for nearly 10 years. We are wildly excited about it," said Webster.

"We fully understand if the choice is between a building and a park, 99 people out of 100 will opt for the park," he said. "I have said to the people of Sydney, give us a chance to see what we can do and how the public will benefit from it, he said.
